analysis.investment_thesis: Chalet Hotels fails both Magic Formula tests: earnings yield of ~3.8% (EBIT INR 736 Cr / EV ~INR 19,575 Cr) is well below my 12% hurdle, and ROCE of 11.1% is below the 20% threshold for a quality business. The hotel is a real-estate-heavy capital destroyer — capex surged to INR 969 Cr in FY25, flipping FCF negative at -14 Cr despite record operating cash flow.
key_strengths: Revenue CAGR of 12.8% over 9 years with strong post-COVID recovery (INR 508 Cr in FY22 to INR 1,718 Cr in FY25)
High EBITDA margins (~44.5% in FY25), reflecting pricing power in premium/upscale hospitality segments
Equity base nearly doubled to INR 3,415 Cr in FY25 (likely QIP/rights), reducing debt from INR 3,005 Cr to INR 2,489 Cr
key_risks: Capital intensity is extreme: INR 969 Cr capex in FY25 with zero free cash flow — returns on incremental capital are unproven
Net profit fell from INR 278 Cr (FY24) to INR 142 Cr (FY25) despite revenue growth, suggesting rising depreciation/interest drag
Hospitality is cyclical and COVID showed a -97% EBIT collapse in FY21; the business generates no economic moat from the Magic Formula lens
red_flags: Earnings yield of ~3.8% (EBIT/EV) is far below my 6% minimum threshold
FCF turned negative (-INR 14 Cr) in FY25 despite INR 950 Cr operating cash flow — all consumed by capex
ROCE of 11.1% below the 20% hurdle; returns insufficient to compensate for capital risk
analysis.detailed_analysis: Chalet Hotels is a well-run hospitality company, but the Magic Formula demands both cheapness and quality — and Chalet delivers neither. Enterprise value of ~INR 19,575 Cr against EBIT of INR 736 Cr yields a meagre 3.8% earnings yield; you would need to pay 26x EBIT to own this business. ROCE of 11.1% confirms the asset-heavy hotel model earns a mediocre spread above cost of capital even in a good year. The massive FY25 investing CF of -INR 1,355 Cr (hotels under construction) means shareholders are funding a long-duration, capital-hungry expansion with no near-term payoff in returns on capital.
